On Monday 12 October 2026, a little before 4 p.m., a man came out of his seat on Goliath, the 200-foot hyper coaster at Six Flags Over Georgia near Atlanta, and died. Cobb County Police named him on 13 October as Hassan Jihad Ibn Kariem, 42, of Atlanta, who worked for Atlanta Public Schools. Police say, from preliminary interviews, that he was ejected from the ride and struck other riders before falling beneath the attraction; several people were hurt. Police have not said why he came out of his seat. That same night Six Flags closed nine similar coasters at parks across the country.

This film rebuilds the afternoon from the riders' and witnesses' own accounts, the train left on the lift hill, the lap bar that holds every rider, the Texas Giant fall of 2013 and what its control panel showed, and how Georgia inspects a ride: once a year, for sixty-five dollars.

As of 14 October: Goliath has no seat belts, only individual lap bars (AP). Bolliger & Mabillard, which built it, says it is investigating. Georgia's Safety Fire Commissioner has inspectors examining the ride; its inspection records are not yet public. Six Flags Over Georgia reopens 16 October with Goliath closed; none of the nine coasters has a reopening date. No cause has been released. The 3D scenes are reconstructions; this film shows no image of the victim and no injury.

snippet.title: GANÓ EL ORO OLÍMPICO… Y SEGÚN ÉL LO TIRÓ AL RÍO
snippet.description:
Años más tarde, ya como Muhammad Ali, contó esta historia en su autobiografía, y se convirtió en una leyenda. Sin embargo, varios amigos suyos aseguraron después que simplemente la había perdido. Lo que sí es cierto es que en su ciudad sufría el racismo como cualquier otro joven negro, a pesar de ser campeón olímpico. En los Juegos de Atlanta 1996, Ali, ya con párkinson, encendió el pebetero olímpico con las manos temblorosas, en una de las imágenes más emocionantes de la historia del deporte. Días después, durante un partido de baloncesto, el presidente del COI le colgó una medalla de oro para reemplazar la perdida. Suscríbete para más historias reales de famosos.
